content.title: Game Preview: Warriors at Sacramento Kings - 4/10/26
content.text: April 9, 202610:12 PM PDTWARRIORS VISIT KINGS ON FRIDAYThe Warriors head to Sacramento to visit the Kings on the second night of a back-to-back on Friday. The Dubs anticipate getting several reinforcements back, headlined by Stephen Curry, who has played two games since a 27-game absence due to a runner’s knee injury. Friday’s game is the penultimate game of the season as Golden State concludes the regular season in Los Angeles against the Clippers, who are a potential Play-In Tournament opponent. LAST TIME OUTThe short-handed Warriors had six players score in double figure in their 119-103 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on Thursday. Brandin Podziemski and Nate Williams led the way with 17 points each. Charles Bassey chipped in for his second consecutive double-double with 12 points and 13 rebounds. LeBron James also had a double-double leading the game with 26 points and 11 assists. All five Laker starters scored in double figures with Ayton finishing as the second-leading scorer with 21 points on 9-for-11 shooting. The Lakers made 16 3-pointers at a 55.2 percent clip compared nine threes and 30.0 percent shooting for the Warriors. »Full StoryVideo Player is loading.Current Time Duration Remaining Time Highlights: Golden State Warriors vs. Los Angeles LakersINJURY & ROSTER NOTESGSW: Stephen Curry (Right Knee; Injury Management), Kristaps Porzingis (Right Knee; Injury Management) and Charles Bassey (Left Ankle; Sprain) are probable. The winner of Friday night’s game will advance to the 2026 NBA Playoffs.Prime Video will have exclusive national coverage of Friday’s game, which is scheduled for a 7 p.m. (PDT) tipoff. NBC Sports Bay Area will continue to provide extensive coverage surrounding games with Warriors Pregame Live and Warriors Postgame Live. The one-hour shows will be hosted by Bonta Hill, alongside Basketball Hall of Famer Chris Mullin and former Warrior Festus Ezeli as analysts. On the radio side, 95.7 The Game and the Warriors Radio Network will broadcast Friday’s game, with play-by-play announcer Tim Roye once again calling the action. In addition to the local radio coverage, the game will also be heard nationally on ESPN Radio.Thrive City will host a Warriors Play-In Watch Party, presented by Kaiser Permanente, on Friday, April 17, beginning at 5:30 p.m. Fans are encouraged to RSVP at thrivecity.com.
